newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar calm as U.S. holiday doldrums hit Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Dollar calm as U.S. holiday doldrums hit Tokyo.

text.p: *Dollar stuck around midday levels in sluggish mid-afternoon trade on Friday as U.S. Independence Day holiday doldrums hit Tokyo market.
*Dollar maintained earlier gains against yen, but operators unwilling to buy back dollars extensively due to lack of convincing buying incentives.
*"The dollar is moving in an extremely tight range this afternoon," a Japanese city bank dealer said. "The dollar/yen rate is not expected to move out of 113.50-114.00."
*Dollar took breather against yen and mark by midday Tokyo after fairly large losses overnight, as activity subdued amid lack of fresh factors and ahead of long weekend in U.S.
*Dollar supported by light short-covering after it broke through support of 114.20 yen overnight, but lack of follow-through purchases limited rise.

*"We are still tired from yesterday's movements. There is nothing special going on except for light short-covering by interbank dealers, who want to square positions ahead of the weekend," a trust bank dealer said.
